It is known for the {{ill|Hōnensai|de|Hōnen-Matsuri|es|Hōnen Matsuri|fa|هونن ماتسوری|fr|Hōnen Matsuri|hr|Hōnen Matsuri|id|Hōnen Matsuri|it|Hōnen Matsuri|ja|豊年祭 (田縣神社)|ms|Hōnen Matsuri|nl|Honen Matsuri|pt|Hōnensai|ro|Hōnen Matsuri|ru|Хонэн-мацури|simple|Hōnensai|sl|Honen Macuri|ta|ஒவுனென் மட்சுறி|uk|Хонен-мацурі|vi|Hōnen Matsuri|qid=Q30924149|lt=Hōnen Festival}} held every March. The character “縣” (agata, ken) is the {{ill|Chinese character forms|ja|字体|mk|Облици на кинеските знаци|zh|漢字的字形|qid=Q137673972|lt=old form}} of “県” (and is sometimes considered a {{ill|Chinese character forms|ja|字体|mk|Облици на кинеските знаци|zh|漢字的字形|qid=Q137673972|lt=variant}}), so it is also written as '''Tagata Shrine''' (田県神社).

== Enshrined deities ==
The enshrined deities are {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Mitoshi-no-Kami}} (みとしのかみ) and Tamahime-no-Mikoto (たまひめのみこと), gods of abundant harvests and the prosperity of descendants. According to shrine tradition, this area was part of the estate of {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Oarata-no-Mikoto}}, where Mitoshi-no-Kami, a god of bountiful crops, was worshiped. Tamahime-no-Mikoto was the daughter of Oarata-no-Mikoto; after her husband’s death, she returned to her parental home, raised her children admirably as a mother, and helped her father cultivate the land. In praise of these merits, she came to be enshrined as a deity.

Within the shrine grounds, many stones shaped like {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=phallic symbols}} are enshrined.

== History ==
The date of foundation is unknown, and it is considered a very old shrine {{citation needed|date=September 2017}}. It is a shrine based on ancient indigenous beliefs and is associated with phallic worship believed to improve {{ill|Male reproductive system|an|Aparato reproductor masculín|ar|جهاز تناسلي It is designated as an Intangible Folk Cultural Property of Komaki City and is read as “Hōnensai” or “Hōnenmatsuri,” also known as the “Henoko Festival.” Men parade while carrying a {{ill|Mikoshi|ar|ميكوشي|cs|Mikoši|de|Mikoshi|es|Mikoshi|fa|میکوشی|fr|Mikoshi|gd|Mikoshi|hr|Mikoshi|hy|Միկոշի|id|Mikoshi|it|Mikoshi|ja|神輿|ko|미코시|mk|Омикоши|ml|മികോഷി|pa|ਮਿਕੋਸ਼ੀ|pl|Mikoshi|pt|Mikoshi|ru|Микоси|simple|Mikoshi|tl|Omikoshi|tr|Mikoshi|uk|Мікосі|zh|神轎|qid=Q979940}} bearing a large phallus called Ōowase-gata, while {{ill|Miko|ar|ميكو (شنتو)|bg|Мико|ca|Miko|cs|Miko|da|Miko|de|Miko (Berufsbezeichnung)|es|Miko|fa|میکو|fi|Miko (šintolaisuus)|fr|Miko (shintoïsme)|hu|Mikó (papnő)|id|Miko|it|Miko|ja|巫女|ko|무녀|nl|Miko (Japan)|or|ମିକୋ|pl|Miko|pt|Miko|ru|Мико|simple|Miko|sk|Miko|sl|Miko (svečenica)|ta|மிக்கோ|te|మికో|th|มิโกะ|tr|Miko|uk|Міко|vi|Miko|zh|巫女|qid=Q1047139}} carry smaller phallic objects. There is a tradition that touching them grants fertility. The Ōowase-gata measures about 60 cm in diameter and over 2 meters in length, and a new one is made each year from {{ill|Chamaecyparis obtusa|arz|تشاميسيباريس اوبتوزا|bg|Chamaecyparis obtusa|ca|Chamaecyparis obtusa|ceb|Chamaecyparis obtusa|cs|Cypřišek tupolistý|da|Solcypres|de|Hinoki-Scheinzypresse|es|Chamaecyparis obtusa|eu|Japoniar altzifre|fa|سرو پاکوتاه|fi|Japaninsypressi|fr|Chamaecyparis obtusa|gl|Chamaecyparis obtusa|hak|Hî-nò-khì|hu|Hinoki hamisciprus|id|Chamaecyparis obtusa|is|Sólsýprus|it|Chamaecyparis obtusa|ja|ヒノキ|ko|편백|ml|ചമേസിപാരിസ് ഒബ്‌ടുസ|no|Solsypress|pl|Cyprysik tępołuskowy|pt|Chamaecyparis obtusa|ru|Кипарисовик туполистный|sv|Japansk ädelcypress|tr|Chamaecyparis obtusa|uk|Кипарисовик туполистий|vi|Chamaecyparis obtusa|war|Chamaecyparis obtusa|zh|日本扁柏|zh_min_nan|Píⁿ-peh|qid=Q917187}} and dedicated to the shrine.

This ritual symbolizes the phallus as “heaven” and the vulva as “earth,” praying that “through blessings from heaven, the land is nourished, resulting in abundant harvests and fertility.” The reason it is held in spring is that it also signifies “the birth of new life.”

Nearby, the Hōnen Festival of {{ill|Ōagata Shrine|abstract|Q135732|fr|Ōagata-jinja|ja|大縣神社|simple|Ōagata Shrine|zh|大縣神社|qid=Q135732}} in {{ill|Inuyama, Aichi|ar|إنوياما (آيتشي)|azb|اینویاما، آیچی|ce|Инуяма|ceb|Inuyama-shi|ckb|ئینویاما، ئایچی|cs|Inujama|de|Inuyama|el|Ινουγιάμα (Άιτσι)|es|Inuyama (Aichi)|eu|Inuyama (Aichi)|fa|اینویاما، آیچی|fi|Inuyama|fr|Inuyama|gl|Inuyama|hy|Ինույամա|id|Inuyama, Aichi|it|Inuyama|ja|犬山市|kk|Инуяма|ko|이누야마시|mdf|Инуяма|mg|Inuyama|mzn|اینویاما، آیچی|nl|Inuyama|pl|Inuyama|pnb|انویامہ|pt|Inuyama|ro|Inuyama|ru|Инуяма|simple|Inuyama, Aichi|sv|Inuyama|tg|Инуяма|th|อินูยามะ|tl|Inuyama, Aichi|tr|Inuyama|tt|Инуяма|uk|Інуяма|ur|انویاما، ایچی|vi|Inuyama, Aichi|war|Inuyama, Aichi|zh|犬山市|zh_classical|犬山市|zh_min_nan|Inuyama-chhī|zh_yue|犬山|qid=Q503411}}—also known as the “Ososo Festival”—forms a pair with this festival; there, floats shaped like {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=vulva}} are paraded.

== Characteristics ==
As souvenirs, candies, chocolates, and {{ill|Objet d'art|be|Аб’ект мастацтва|es|Objet d'art|fr|Objet d'art|ja|オブジェ|ko|오브제|qid=Q7075109}} shaped like phallic symbols are sold.

In recent years, it has become extremely popular with foreigners, and many foreign tourists visit.

Only on the day of the Hōnen Festival, multiple {{ill|Parking lot|an|Aparcamento|ar|موقف سيارات|az|Avtodayanacaq|ckb|پارکی ئۆتۆمۆبیل|cs|Parkoviště|da|Parkeringsplads|de|Parkplatz|eo|Parkumejo|es|Estacionamiento|et|Parkla|fa|پارکینگ خودرو|fi|Pysäköintialue|fr|Parking|fy|Parkearterrein|he|חניון|hr|Parkiralište|id|Pelataran parkir|it|Parcheggio|ja|駐車場|ko|주차장|ku|Otopark|la|Area stativa|lb|Parkplaz|mk|Паркиралиште|pl|Parking|pt|Parque de estacionamento|ru|Стоянка (сооружение)|sh|Parkiralište|simple|Parking lot|sk|Parkovisko|sv|Parkeringsplats|ta|வாகன நிறுத்துமிடம்|th|ลานจอดรถ|tr|Otopark|uk|Автостоянка|vi|Bãi đỗ xe|wa|Parkigne|zh|停車場|zh_yue|停車場|qid=Q6501349}} are set up near the shrine.
